statement: Ibn Mas'ud: the first seven to show their Islam; the Prophet protected by Abu Talib, Abu Bakr by his people; the rest dressed in iron coats in the sun; all gave in outwardly except Bilal, who was handed to boys who dragged him through Makkah as he said 'Ahad, Ahad'.
notes: Machine-checked. Graded hasan (al-Albani: hasan sahih; al-Arna'ut: hasan). That Bilal was Abyssinian and a slave is from the Seerah.

statement: Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal; Umar said 'Abu Bakr is our master and he freed our master'.
He passed the family of Yasir under torture and said 'Patience, family of Yasir, your appointed place is Paradise'.
notes: Recorded by al-Hakim and others; graded hasan sahih by al-Albani (Fiqh as-Sirah), from memory. Narrated with attribution until the reviewer confirms a graded reference.

statement: Sumayyah was killed and was the first martyr in Islam.
Ammar was tortured until he uttered words of disbelief, and came to the Prophet in distress.
notes: Reported by the commentators as the occasion of 16:106.

statement: Qur'an 16:106 exempts one who is forced while his heart is at rest in faith.

Khabbab asked him in the shade of the Ka'bah to pray for them; he sat up red-faced and spoke of earlier believers combed with iron and sawn in two, and of the rider from Sana'a to Hadramawt; 'but you are in haste'.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked. 'But you are in haste' is in 3612. That Khabbab was a blacksmith is in other narrations.

statement: Ibn Mas'ud: camel entrails were laid on his back in prostration at the Ka'bah by the most wretched of them; they laughed; Fatimah removed it.
notes: Machine-checked. The narration continues with his supplication against those involved; left for the chapter on Badr.

statement: Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt strangled him with his garment while he prayed; Abu Bakr pushed him away saying 'Would you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah?'
notes: Machine-checked. Abu Bakr's words quote Qur'an 40:28.

statement: Abu Jahl swore to tread on his neck in prayer, approached, and turned back saying there was between them a trench of fire, terror and wings.
notes: Content found in the Muslim dataset by text search. Abd al-Baqi number from memory.

statement: Khabbab was a blacksmith in Makkah and experienced pressure to renounce Muhammad; he also reported the believers' suffering to the Prophet.
notes: Blacksmith work and the demand that he disbelieve Muhammad are in Bukhari 2091; his report of the believers' suffering is in Bukhari 3852. Number and English wording checked in the local dataset; human review remains required.
